passage: SOURCES_D row SIM03 (abstract): class-prediction performance assessed on the data used to build the rule; independent validation is required.
faulty: Ridge regression of response on [standardised expression, standardised clinical covariates] (penalty fixed at lambda = number of columns) is fitted on all 80 patients; the Pearson correlation between its fitted values and the observed response, on the same 80 patients, is the statistic (resubstitution). Claim holds when r >= 0.30.
fixed: Same model; predictions for each patient come from 10-fold cross-validation (patients in the held-out fold are not used in fitting or standardising); r is the Pearson correlation between these held-out predictions and the observed response.
estimand: Faulty: correlation between the fitted values and the outcomes of the patients that built the model. Fixed: correlation between predictions and outcomes in new patients.
model_family: Ridge regression with a fixed penalty on the concatenated standardised blocks. Chosen by me: the source names no model; fixed penalty avoids tuning (stays L1.1).
sizes_note: Source sizes: not stated in the text I read. 80 x (1500 + 8) is a realistic small clinical array study; low check cost. Dependence of the error on n or p: not stated.
exploited_structure: Many more genes than patients, so fitted values can track the training outcomes from noise.

structure_statistic.note_value_source: source states none: SIM03 sizes were not available to me; 18.75 = 1500 genes / 80 patients, this brief's own ratio

notes: Differs from B2B-01 in statistic (correlation vs R-squared), data structure (two predictor blocks) and sample-size regime (80 patients, 1500 genes). Prognostic/continuous variant as in B2B-01.
